beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "The numbers I found on my Thursdays: I've been covering more of the material costs than we ever agreed to. He doesn't know."

options.text: So what does telling him honestly actually look like?
Just quietly stop covering it and see what happens.
Maybe don't mention it at all.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I don't want it to sound like an accusation. I just want it fixed."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: Start with an honest look at yourself, not at him — then it won't land like an accusation.
Make sure he feels as guilty as possible.
Fairness isn't really the point here.

elaboration: Justice starts as a mirror pointed at you first — an honest look at your own part in it, before it ever becomes about assigning blame.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "But we never actually wrote the cost split down anywhere. Is it even fair to bring it up now?"

options.text: Nothing needed to be written down for it to be worth fixing now.
If it's not written down, it doesn't count.
Bringing it up now is too late to matter.

elaboration: Justice was never waiting on a rulebook — it acts because something's simply right, and the imbalance catching up with you now is exactly the card's timing.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Alright. I'll bring the actual numbers, not just the feeling, and we'll split it evenly from here."
